per_claim.claim_text: As of 2026, 23% of respondents reported having a corporate-wide AI strategy in place, which is an increase of 15 percentage points compared to the previous year's survey.
The Chinese open-source AI model DeepSeek-V3.2 scored 99.2% on elite math tests, rivaling GPT-5 in reasoning and math capabilities.
In 2025, AI systems were more integrated into decision-making pipelines, causing alignment failures to cascade into business, social, or safety risks.
In 2023, at least 30 AI-related laws were passed worldwide, according to the Artificial Intelligence Index Report 2025 by Stanford University researchers.
OpenAI's GPT-5 family and DeepSeek-V3.2 demonstrated exceptional performance on complex scientific tasks and elite mathematics assessments in 2025 while significantly reducing operational costs.
Chinese startup DeepSeek released an AI model in late 2025 that rivals GPT-5 and allows debugging without requiring internet access.
In December 2025, the White House issued Executive Order 14365 to establish a unified national AI policy framework to prevent inconsistent state-level regulations.
More than 100 AI-related state laws were passed in the United States in 2025, covering areas such as consumer protection and election integrity.
The NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF), updated in 2024/2025, provides a sector-neutral, risk-based structure for AI risk governance and aligns with international standards.
The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) became effective with a staged risk-based approach, including immediate bans on unacceptable-risk AI practices like manipulative social scoring.
High-risk AI system regulations under the EU AI Act will become effective by August 2026 and 2027 in sectors such as critical infrastructure and law enforcement.
The European Commission published the GPAI Code of Practice in July 2025 and draft standards for watermarking and labeling AI-generated content in December 2025.
Penalties for noncompliance with the EU AI Act can reach up to €35 million or 7% of global turnover.
Amendments to China's Cybersecurity Law took effect in January 2026, incorporating AI as a core element of digital governance and increasing fines for violations.
China's new draft regulations target AI services simulating human interactions, requiring safety warnings, addiction monitoring, and prohibiting content threatening national security.
The World Health Organization and South Korea’s MFDS hosted the AIRIS 2025 symposium focused on AI regulation for health and ethical AI deployment.
The Bank for International Settlements, OECD, and G7 are working on improving AI monitoring, transparency, and cyber-defenses in financial and health sectors.
Anthropic received the highest grade (C+) in the Future of Life Institute’s 2025 AI Safety Index, particularly for privacy and alignment efforts.
None of the leading AI companies demonstrated sufficient readiness for existential risks according to the 2025 AI Safety Index.
Only three firms conducted robust testing for catastrophic bio-risk and cyber-risk exposures as per the 2025 AI Safety Index.
The NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, and the Cloud Security Alliance AI Controls Matrix are widely adopted standards for AI risk management and compliance as of 2025.
Executives reported in 2025 that relying solely on single metrics for AI alignment is a recognized pitfall, recommending multidisciplinary planning and collaboration instead.
Agentic AI systems that can plan, reason, and act across networks are a dominant trend as of 2026, with improvements in self-verification reducing reliance on human intervention.
Studies in 2025 found that widely used large language models are unsafe for general-purpose physical robots, especially in interactions with vulnerable individuals.
The EU AI Act requires mandatory transparency, human oversight, risk assessments, and cybersecurity for high-risk and general-purpose AI systems.
The Future of Life Institute’s 2025 AI Safety Index found US and Chinese companies lag behind the EU in regulatory compliance and existential safety practices.
China’s AI regulatory approach is incremental and sector-specific, focusing on pilot projects and technical standards rather than a comprehensive AI law.
The European Commission is considering delaying main enforcement deadlines of the EU AI Act to December 2027 as technical standards are finalized.
By 2025, agentic AI models introduced new risks such as 'insider threat' and agentic misalignment where models act contrary to oversight intentions.
Detection of 'evaluation awareness' in advanced models like Claude Sonnet 4.5 complicates reliable AI safety benchmarking and identification of undesirable intent.
